clue.text: Scottish location not without its advocates?

definitions.text: Scottish location not without its advocates?

parts.words: Scottish location not without its advocates?
parts.note: advocates in court wear wigs, so a place well supplied with them is a settlement of wigs, a Scottish town split into two words

explanation.surface: A Scottish place that has plenty of lawyers speaking up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: a WIG TOWN. Scottish advocates (barristers) wear wigs, so a town 'not without its advocates' has wigs; Wigtown is a real town in south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Wigtown is a small town in Galloway, a real Scottish place name.

clue.text: Old-time yarn spinner and lexicographer

explanation.surface: An old storyteller who also compiled a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: A webster was an old word for a weaver, who spins yarn; Noah Webster compiled the American dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word meant a weaver, and Noah Webster compiled the famous American dictionary.

clue.text: Upset King George going round making a pig of oneself

indicators.note: round means the word going circles the turned letters
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Ousting King George by going round him while overeating.
explanation.walkthrough: GR stands for Georgius Rex; 'Upset' turns it to RG, a down-clue reversal, and 'round' wraps the going around it. The surface's 'going' looks like part of the story about the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorging is eating greedily, stuffing oneself.

clue.text: Minute portion for the snow-leopard

explanation.surface: A tiny piece of food set aside for a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: An ounce is a small weight; it is also another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: A small weight of a sixteenth of a pound gives the first sense; the second is an old name for a Himalayan cat.

clue.text: Kilt on backwards at the cathedral? Hardly

indicators.note: backwards means the letters of kilt on are read in reverse

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Someone wearing a kilt the wrong way round in a cathedral is improbable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' makes NOTLIK; Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England, which is all 'the cathedral' needs to give.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a firm refusal or doubt, like 'scarcely' or 'no chance'.

clue.text: Sought-after tree round the bend

indicators.note: the tree's letters go round the bend, enclosing it

parts.note: a poplar is a tall tree
U is a U-bend, a curve shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A much-wanted tree growing around a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts U inside POPLAR, between the P and the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sought-after is in demand, the sense of widely liked.

clue.text: Knock up one's capital

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for knock is read from the bottom

parts.note: a rap is a knock
one's stands for one is, I plus S, here written IS

explanation.surface: Making someone pregnant in a big city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP into PAR, and 'one's' gives IS ('one is'). The surface plays on 'knock up', British slang for waking someone and also for making pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Doctrinal believer converted in the past

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters of in the past are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who switched religions long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges IN THE PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheist holds that God and the universe are one, a religious doctrine.

clue.text: Brief inspection suggesting double-vision?

parts.note: the vision is doubled: one word for seeing
and a second word for seeing

explanation.surface: A quick look that makes you see two of things.
explanation.walkthrough: Two words for using one's eyes side by side make the answer: 'double-vision' is two vision words.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick glance or brief inspection is an informal phrase for having a peek.

clue.text: Forbear to keep a little brother in check

indicators.note: to keep means the word for check holds the brother inside it

parts.note: to rein in is to check
Fra is the short form of the Italian for brother, used for friars

explanation.surface: Holding back so as to keep a younger sibling under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little brother' suggests a younger sibling, but it is the abbreviated title Fra, used for Italian friars; 'to keep' sets it inside the check word.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to forbear, to hold back from doing something.

clue.text: Title apparently excluding one letter

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'bar none'
T is simply one letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A heading that seems to leave out a single character.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as BAR ONE T, 'except one T'; 'apparently' signals that the answer only looks like that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank, a title below baron.

clue.text: Hang up after breaking the engagement?

explanation.surface: Putting the phone down once the wedding is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: once an engagement is broken the ring comes off the finger.
explanation.definitionFit: To end a phone call is to put the receiver down; a broken engagement has its token band removed.

clue.text: Palatial gardens of 5 down

parts.note: 5 down is the French capital; the clue asks for its famous gardens beside the former royal palace

explanation.surface: The grounds of a palace in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is PARIS, so the clue wants the gardens there that once belonged to a royal palace by the Louvre.
explanation.definitionFit: These gardens in central Paris were laid out for the vanished royal palace of the same name.

clue.text: A shoe-repairing prophet

indicators.note: repairing is fixing, putting the letters of a shoe back into a new working order

explanation.surface: A biblical seer who mends footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairing' rearranges the letters of A SHOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosea is one of the minor prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Correct observance we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for observance is taken by its spoken sound

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial observance

explanation.surface: Getting a ritual done properly, by report.
explanation.walkthrough: RITE (an observance) is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct and its synonym both mean accurate or true.

clue.text: Otto's home set in good taste

indicators.note: set means arranged, putting the letters of Otto's home into a new order

explanation.surface: Otto's house is decorated tastefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges OTTOS HOME; here the S of Otto's counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means delicious, pleasing to the palate.

clue.text: Notion held by eccentric uncle from the old Greek

indicators.note: held by means the notion is gripped inside the other letters
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of uncle are rearranged

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: An odd relative has a concept borrowed from an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' makes EUCLN, and 'held by' places the notion inside it, between L and N. 'from the old Greek' defines an adjective meaning Euclid's.
explanation.definitionFit: Euclid was the ancient Greek geometer, so the adjective means derived from him.

clue.text: Figure on the accuracy of an abacus, perhaps

definitions.text: the accuracy of an abacus, perhaps

explanation.surface: Relying on a bead frame for a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is to rely on; the second takes the words literally, an abacus being something you can count on to count.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on is the idiom's sense; an abacus is a device for counting, so its reliability is literal.

clue.text: Bury a food upsetting your health

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the letters of bury a food are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Burying some food that does your stomach no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges BURY A FOOD; the definition borrows its sense from the whole phrase, 'upsetting your health'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes anything harmful to one's wellbeing, the opposite of wholesome.

clue.text: Feller's bargain for a dollar?

parts.note: a feller is one who cuts trees; a buck is a dollar, so a tool for the woodsman bought for a buck

explanation.surface: A man getting a deal for a single dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feller' looks like 'fellow' but is a tree-feller; 'buck' is slang for a dollar, so the tool is a buck's saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucksaw is a framed saw used for cutting logs.

clue.text: Dope to obtain a material saving on wear and tear

definitions.text: a material saving on wear and tear

parts.note: dope is slang for a drug
to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Getting drugs to cut down on wear.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUG then GET; 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A drugget is a coarse cloth laid over a carpet to protect it.

clue.text: March right in to work

indicators.note: in puts the letter for right inside the word to

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching rightward on the way to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month but is a verb; 'in' places R inside the first word, and op (opus) is a stock crossword word for a work.
explanation.definitionFit: To troop is to walk together in a group, as soldiers do.

clue.text: Boring thing spoken about on a satellite course

indicators.note: about means the word for spoken goes round the boring thing

parts.note: oral means spoken
a drill bit is the boring part of a drill

explanation.surface: A dull thing someone talked about concerning a satellite's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means drilling, not dull: the drill's working part goes inside the spoken word, signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital path is the circuit a satellite follows round a planet.

clue.text: Obtained satisfaction making Peel sad

indicators.note: making means forming the letters of Peel sad into something new

explanation.surface: Feeling content at making a statesman named Peel unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges PEEL SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pleased is to feel gratified or content.

clue.text: Layer of grass?

parts.note: read the clue as a thing one lays down or lies on, a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Something laid down from grass, like turf.
explanation.walkthrough: Couch grass is a common weed; the same word is a sofa, something one lies on, and to couch is to lay down, so 'Layer' is one who lays.
explanation.definitionFit: Couch grass is a creeping weed, and the furniture of the same name is where people lie.

clue.text: Cannot hold a number indefensible

indicators.note: hold means the letters for cannot keep a number in their grip

parts.note: unable means cannot
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone unable to keep a figure in an argument that cannot be defended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannot' looks like the start of a sentence, but it is a synonym piece; 'hold' puts the number inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A position that cannot be defended, in argument or war, is indefensible.

clue.text: They resort to American ex expressions of hesitancy

parts.note: US means American
er is a sound of hesitation, so several are ers

explanation.surface: Former Americans who keep hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: US then ERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Users are people who resort to or make use of something.

clue.text: Tender shark

explanation.surface: A gentle shark.
explanation.walkthrough: To nurse is to tend; the nurse shark is a slow bottom-dwelling species.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is to care for them; there is also a species called the nurse shark.

clue.text: Italian gentleman has Susan's initial disregard

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of Susan's name

parts.note: to ignore is to disregard

explanation.surface: An Italian man pays no attention to what Susan says first.
explanation.walkthrough: S, Susan's first letter, then IGNORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Signore is the Italian form of address for a man, like sir or mister.

clue.text: Of mineral content it is found in combustible heaps

indicators.note: is found in places the word it inside the heaps

parts.note: pyres are heaps of wood built to burn

explanation.surface: Something mineral turns up inside burning piles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is found in' sets the little word inside the burning heaps; pyrites is iron sulphide, so 'mineral content' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron pyrites is a common sulphide ore, fool's gold.

clue.text: Gives a scornful look backing horses

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at punters who bet on racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a horse's anatomy: the ridge at the top of the back between the shoulder blades.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare contemptuously is to shrivel with a look; the high point of a horse's back carries the same name.

clue.text: Provoked by want in the first place

parts.note: want here means need
led means went first, at the front

explanation.surface: Annoyed because of a basic need.
explanation.walkthrough: NEED (want) then LED (was in the first place); 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means irritated or goaded, much as a sharp jab annoys.
